summary: Master currency risk management in aid operations. Learn hedging, treasury policy, and donor compliance to protect humanitarian budgets. Enroll today.
lede: Currency and Foreign Exchange Risk Management in Aid Operations helps professionals identify, measure, and mitigate the financial effects of currency fluctuations across humanitarian and development programs. You will learn to move from reactive variance analysis to proactive treasury management that supports purchasing power, program continuity, and donor reporting requirements. The course covers exposure identification, Value at Risk calculations, multi-currency budgeting, hedging strategy design, IFRS 21 reporting, and internal control implementation. By the end, you will have developed an FX risk register, automated tracking approach, and strategic hedging roadmap suited to aid operations facing inflation, market shocks, and limited banking infrastructure.
audienceIntro: This intermediate-level program is essential for finance and operations professionals responsible for the financial integrity of international aid programs.
modules: Aid Operations and Global Currency Volatility
Measurement and Quantification of FX Risk
Spot Markets and Forward Contract Strategies
Cash Flow Forecasting and Liquidity Management
Digital Payments and Mobile Money Integration
Strategic FX Policy and Stakeholder Communication
prerequisites: Participants should have a foundational understanding of financial accounting and experience working within the finance or operations department of an international organization. Familiarity with basic spreadsheet functions (Excel) and standard grant management cycles is required.
